title: Emerald Velvet — Embossed Members' Crest
description: A deep emerald leather-textured ground carries a monochromatic embossed crest and italic copperplate date, framed by a hairline blind-deboss border — the precise visual register of a Soho House dinner menu or an Annabel's event card translated into a presentation cover.
philosophy: This template exists for presentations that must feel like printed matter rather than software. It refuses colour variety, layered hierarchy, and digital brightness in favour of tactile illusion, severe restraint, and the authority of a single emblem. The speaker it serves is confident enough to let one crest and one date command a room in silence. It is built for audiences who recognise understated luxury because they inhabit it every day.
goodFor: Private members' club event announcements and seasonal menu reveal covers
Luxury hospitality gala or charity auction opening title slides
High-end brand heritage storytelling requiring a single-crest cover moment
Annual dinner programmes and exclusive awards ceremony openers
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring dense data layers
Multi-section agenda slides with more than three lines of text
Startup pitch decks demanding energetic, high-contrast visual variety
Conference presentations where speaker headshots and bios share the canvas
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a private-club dinner menu lifted from the press — monochromatic, tactile, and completely still. A single embossed crest commands the center with heraldic authority, surrounded by deliberate silence; the velvet ground is a material presence, not a backdrop. Composition is symmetrical and monastic, the hairline border reading as physical blind-deboss rather than a digital rule. Avoid layered hierarchy, glowing highlights, or any suggestion of software brightness — the illusion of printed matter is the only goal.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed emerald ground with no header band or footer bar — the canvas bleeds to all four edges. A hairline blind-deboss border sits inset from every edge, functioning as the sole compositional frame rather than a grid-line. Content locks to a single centered vertical axis: embossed crest at mid-canvas, deck title in a tight band directly below it, and an italic copperplate date as the only secondary element beneath that. All remaining canvas is intentionally empty; negative space is load-bearing structure, not leftover margin.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the inside spread of a private members' club dinner programme — authoritative stillness, as though pressed onto heavy cotton stock. Compositional rhythm is sparse and centrally anchored: text is a solitary event within the space, not a filling of it. A monochromatic embossed ornament crowns the content block, lending ceremonial gravity without ornamental excess. Avoid any suggestion of software UI chrome, digital brightness, or layered visual hierarchy — severe restraint is the entire statement.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with content occupying cols 3–10, yielding roughly 15% outer margins on each side to echo a printed card's breathing room. A hairline rule separates a small centered ornament at the top of the content zone from the body text block below; a matching hairline closes the block at the foot. Section or page index sits bottom-right in the smallest typographic register, flush inside the blind-deboss border frame. No header band — the leather-textured ground bleeds edge-to-edge behind all elements.
